title: The hazelnut
hookLine: Julian is shown all that is made as small as a hazelnut, kept because God loves it

cards: Hold out one hand, palm up. Empty. Now set something very small in it in your mind: a bead, a seed, a nut, something you could lose in a coat pocket and never notice.

Julian of Norwich says that in one of her showings God put a thing like that in the palm of her hand. Round as a ball, small enough to close her fingers over. And when she asked what it was, an answer came.

teach.h: A LITTLE THING IN HER PALM.
teach.b: First, the thing in her hand. In Grace Warrack's translation, Julian says she was shown "a little thing, the quantity of an hazel-nut, in the palm of my hand."
She looked at it with what she calls the eye of her understanding, and wondered what it could be. The answer came: "It is all that is made." Everything, in a shape small enough to hold.
Second, her fear. Julian wonders how it can last at all. It's so small, she thinks, it might suddenly fall into nothing.
That's an honest worry, and an old one: the world can feel that fragile. Third, the answer. She is told that it lasts, and always will, because God loves it.
Not because it's strong, or large, or useful, or earned it. It is kept because it is loved. Fourth, what she sees in it.

teach.h: IT IS ALL THAT IS MADE.
teach.b: Julian says she saw three things in this little thing: that God made it, that God loves it, and that God keeps it.

teach.h: SO SMALL IT MIGHT FALL TO NOTHING.

teach.b: She doesn't leave it as a lesson about the universe.
She goes straight on to speak of us, and of why we look for rest in things so small. For her, it's the same promise as all shall be well, made small enough to carry.

how: Catholics who pray with Julian's Revelations of Divine Love return to the hazelnut passage in retreats and spiritual reading, and some keep a small stone or nut as a reminder of it.

o: a symbol Julian used for her own small, humble soul
Julian's picture of all that is made, small in her hand
the food Julian lived on in her cell by the church

s: the hazelnut lasts because it is strong
Julian is told it lasts because God loves it.

the hazelnut stands for one small thing Julian owned

games.q: you're Julian. in your palm is all that is made, so small it looks as if it could fall into nothing. what answer do you hear?
o: it lasts because God loves it.
it lasts because it is stronger than it looks.
it will pass soon, so let it go.
games.why: she is told it lasts, and always will, because God loves it. made, loved, kept.

practice: Rest your open hand on your knee with something small in it, a nut, a stone, a button, and look at it the way Julian did, with attention, not hurry.

Notice how easily it could roll away, then let it stand for everything: the world, the people you love, yourself. If you pray, hold her three words, made, loved, kept; if not, just keep the hand open and steady.

wordCard.voice: The hazelnut. Julian's showing of all that is made, small enough to sit in her palm, and lasting because God loves it. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: kept because loved. That was the whole answer to Julian's fear. See you tomorrow.
